purpose: decide what goes into a release and when, so that scope, risk and dependencies are agreed before the work is frozen
entry_criteria: Candidate changes and their status are known
Release calendar and freeze rules exist
Dependencies between teams and systems are listed
procedure: List the candidate changes with owners, readiness and risk.
Check dependencies between changes, teams, services and migrations; order or bundle accordingly.
Choose the scope the team can finish and test; defer the rest with a reason.
Pick the date and window against freezes, peak periods and on-call capacity.
Agree the rollout approach (progressive or all at once) and the communication plan.
Publish the plan and the scope-freeze point; changes after the freeze need explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Each change has an owner and readiness status
Dependencies are ordered or called out
The window avoids freezes and peaks
Freeze date and exception process are published
validation_method: Release manager and product owner agreement.

validation.check: check each change in scope has a merged or ready pull request and tests
compare the window with the freeze calendar

failure_modes.detection: A change needs another not in scope
failure_modes.response: Add the dependency or defer both

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: The plan includes six changes. One requires a database migration owned by another team, so both ship together on a Tuesday window outside the month-end freeze; a seventh change is deferred as not tested in time.
